# Willpower @ Stage 7 — Sentential & Faith

> developed 2026-07-24.

## Expression on this line

Willpower at Order 6 is creedal discipline: self-regulation is experienced as a sacred duty,
a moral obligation that binds regardless of situation or personal desire. "I must control
myself because it is right" — discipline is experienced as a proposition about moral reality,
not just a practical technique.

The key advance is that self-regulation now has a *moral structure* — it is experienced as
duty, not just technique. The individual controls themselves not because the technique works
(Order 5) but because it is morally required.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** the felt moral obligation of self-discipline — duty experienced as binding.
- **UR:** reliable, duty-driven self-regulation that persists even when the technique seems
  unnecessary.
- **LL:** the shared moral discipline culture — the community's norms about duty and
  self-obligation.
- **LR:** the moral texts and authorities that supply the duty-claims.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** duty-rigidity — the individual who cannot relax discipline even when
  the situation demands flexibility.
- **Dark allergy:** duty-absence — the individual who cannot or will not experience self-
  regulation as morally required.
- **Golden addiction:** claiming to have achieved reflective self-discipline (Order 7) when
  actually just reciting duty-claims.
- **Golden allergy:** refusing to engage with duty-based discipline because it seems
  "unthinking."

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Duty-driven self-regulation:** the individual controls themselves because it is morally
  required, not just because it works.
- **Moral structure of discipline:** self-regulation is experienced as a moral obligation.
- **Authority-based discipline:** discipline is justified by reference to moral authority.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:** Kant, *Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals* (duty as moral self-regulation);
Durkheim, *Moral Education* (discipline as sacred duty).
**Open joints:** How does duty-based discipline shade into reflective self-discipline
(Order 7)?
**Research debt:** pairs with `06-nominal-rule` (codified discipline) and `08-preoperational`
(evaluative self-discipline).
